bioghist.head: Biographical/Historical Information
bioghist.p: The Board for Waterworks and Wastewater Works Operators was established in 1971 to regulate individuals who operate water and wastewater treatment facilities. The Board issues licenses to operate waterworks or wastewater works. It also protects public health, welfare and property, conserves and protects water resources of the Commonwealth and requires examination of operators and certification of their competence to supervise and operate waterworks and wastewater works. In 2009, oversight for Onsite Sewage System Professionals was added to the responsibilities of the board and the name of the board was changed. The Dept. of Professional and Occupational Regulation provides administrative support to the board.

odd.p: These records are part of the Virginia Dept. of Professional and Occupational Regulation record group (RG 17)

Electronic records in this collection are read-only and are only available in the Archives Research Room at the Library of Virginia. A file list is available through the online catalog entry and the link below in the finding aid. Copies are free of charge and may be requested while using the collection in-house. Copies may also be requested by contacting Archives Reference Services. Processing will take from 4-8 weeks.

accessrestrict.p: Meeting attachments must be reviewed for personal information and redacted prior to serving.

scopecontent.p: Minutes and related attachments documenting the meetings, activities, discussions, policy decisions, and recommendations of the Virginia Board for Waterworks and Wastewater Works Operators. Includes official board minutes, as well as draft minutes, committee meeting minutes, agendas and other meeting materials. May also include informal fact finding hearing minutes, correspondence, legislation, regulations and reports.

Electronic records often contain board meeting packets with various attachments and draft minutes, while paper records often include minutes only. There may be some duplication between paper and electronic records. For transfers prior to 2012, records of individual boards were accessioned separately. After this, transfers of records (records starting in 2008) included all boards, which were accessioned under one accession number. There is a separate finding aid for the later transfers (link to finding aid below).
